title: From Kills to Kilometers: Using Centrographic Techniques and Rational Choice Theory for Geographical Profiling of Serial Killers

source.pdf_page_offset_note: Physical page 1 is the standalone Summary; physical pages 2-26 contain the internally numbered 1-25 paper.

notes: All 26 text pages and all 26 rendered pages were reviewed in order.
Six full-page JPEG contact proxies and two formula/table crop proxies stayed below 450000 bytes; no original page PNG entered model context.

context_sources.summary: FBI definitions and geographic-profiling studies motivate linkage, anchor, circle, and proximity claims.
Wikipedia and newspaper sources supply event addresses and dates later converted to coordinates.
The 40-reference bibliography covers geographical profiling, rational choice, crime-pattern theory, statistics, mapping, and historical cases.

inputs: ordered locations and times of crimes attributed to one serial offender
candidate geographic hunting area and grid
centrographic damping parameter or rational-choice kernel assumptions
outputs: error-distance, Hit Score, and Search Area evaluations
decisions: where police search for the offender
which area may contain the next event
whether case assumptions make either model usable

section_map.summary: The standalone Summary moves from the police task and sparse crime-site inputs through behavioral assumptions, two complementary models, case tests, two metrics, omitted geography, and a bounded starting-point recommendation.

The titled Abstract repeats the dual-model contract more compactly: familiar-area behavior motivates centrographic motion and rational-choice surfaces, followed by holdout comparison and parameter sensitivity.
The Introduction defines the scarce-data challenge, states the two prediction targets, previews simulation on partial historical series, and gives an explicit Section 3 to Section 7 roadmap.
The background narrows serial murder, gives empirical home-proximity evidence, explains anchor-point clustering, and states the unmoved-residence premise used by geographical profiling.
Previous work connects journey-to-crime decay, circle and buffer-zone approaches, centroid analysis, and rational-choice crime-pattern theory to the paper's two adaptations.
The centrographic background treats crime sites as a time-ordered spatial series and introduces kinematic vocabulary as an analogy for a moving centroid rather than a literal behavioral law.
The assumption subsection fixes correct linkage, chronological order, one relevant trajectory, a usable time scale, and a centroid whose motion contains predictive information.

The model derives the running centroid, event and centroid velocities, a momentum-style recurrence, acceleration extrapolation, logistic decay functions, beta selection, and a diamond-shaped next-site region.
The rational-choice background distinguishes bounded purposeful selection from moral approval and converts avoidance of capture, familiarity, and opportunity into location-dependent choice costs.

The theory subsection moves from utility over location probabilities and characteristics to an implicit choice function, then specializes it to binary prior-use risk, distance decay, sequence likelihood, and an anchor posterior.
The practice subsection discretizes geography, scans possible homes, produces a jeopardy surface, and extends the same kernel-likelihood interface to a ranked next-crime surface.
The Data section names public web and newspaper sources, converts street addresses to latitude-longitude pairs, preserves crime order, and presents the Berkowitz example table before simulation.

The centrographic results repeatedly hold out kill j, fit on kills 1 through j-1, report Manhattan error for Hillside Strangler events, tabulate acceleration regressions, and display predicted diamonds.
The RSC results define Hit Score and Search Area, then compare Berkowitz Bronx and Yonkers homes with the Buono-Bianchi home using tables and categorical jeopardy maps.

The combined section places centrographic and RSC outputs beside one another for later-event prediction and uses the DC Sniper case to expose incompatible repeated-location and same-day-event assumptions.

The Discussion interprets successes and failures separately, questions acceleration fit and beta sensitivity, contrasts home locations, acknowledges contrived boundaries, and proposes practical revisions without hiding failed cases.
The Executive Summary translates both models into police inputs, contour and diamond outputs, search-area use, strengths, weaknesses, computational needs, and a joint-use recommendation.
The reference list documents geographical profiling, criminology, rational choice, statistical methods, mapping sources, and case-data provenance while leaving implementation code unavailable.

assumptions.summary: All supplied events are correctly linked to one offender.
The offender has one relevant and stationary anchor point during the modeled series.
Serial offenders prefer familiar areas near home or prior sites.
Chronological centroid motion contains information about the next event.
Elapsed times are positive and comparable across the sequence.
Longitude and latitude acceleration can be fitted independently.
The selected beta makes motion decay on a useful time scale.
A rational offender chooses locations through observable site characteristics and avoidance costs.
Previously used cells can be excluded and inverse distance approximates location preference.
Candidate homes have a uniform prior over the chosen hunting area.
Historical prefix likelihoods can be mixed to rank the next site.
Error distance, Hit Score, and Search Area meaningfully represent police performance.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Historical crime series are treated as linked, ordered observations with sparse sample sizes.
Crime coordinates are converted into running centroids and finite-difference velocities.
The RSC model discretizes a hunting area and encodes whether each cell was used previously.
Street addresses and dates from public sources are converted to latitude-longitude pairs and ordered in Table 1.
Centrographic testing repeatedly removes the next event from the spatial prefix.
RSC evaluation defines a case-specific hunting area whose size directly enters Search Area.

models.summary: The running spatial mean interface retains running crime-site centroid: Update the mean location after the jth event.
The centroid time derivative interface retains centroid velocity: Represent the time rate of change of the running centroid.
The mass-scaled centroid velocity interface retains centroid momentum: Scale centroid velocity by the number of events in the physical analogy.
The finite-difference event velocity interface retains new-event velocity: Measure the new event's displacement from the previous centroid per elapsed time.
The unit-mass event momentum interface retains new-event momentum: Assign unit mass to the newly added event in the analogy.
The inelastic momentum recurrence interface retains momentum update: Combine the previous centroid motion with the incoming event motion.
The recursive centroid velocity interface retains centroid velocity recurrence: Compute the updated centroid velocity explicitly.
The damped kinematic forecast interface retains future center: Forecast the center using current location, velocity, and fitted acceleration.
The asymptotic zero velocity interface retains long-run stopping constraint: Force the extrapolated center's velocity to vanish at long horizons.
The local linear scaling interface retains short-run velocity scaling: Recover ordinary constant-velocity motion near the forecast origin.
The local quadratic scaling interface retains short-run acceleration scaling: Recover ordinary constant-acceleration displacement near the forecast origin.
The logistic velocity damping interface retains velocity damping function: Blend local linear motion with long-run stopping.
The squared logistic acceleration damping interface retains acceleration damping function: Blend local quadratic acceleration with long-run stopping.
The mean-interval damping parameter interface retains paper beta selection: Set the damping horizon from the series' mean inter-event time.
The utility over probabilities and characteristics interface retains location-choice utility: Represent preferences over location probabilities and site characteristics.
The choice-probability constraint interface retains probability simplex: Constrain location-choice probabilities to a simplex.
The unconstrained stated FOC interface retains paper first-order condition: Retain the paper's stated optimality condition for later audit.
The characteristic-conditioned choice interface retains implicit choice function: Express each location probability as a function of all site characteristics.
The binary visited-location characteristic interface retains binary prior-use risk: Mark cells already used in the observed sequence.
The inverse-distance normalized kernel interface retains distance-buffer kernel: Score an unused candidate inversely with distance from a possible home while imposing a buffer.
The kernel-conditioned event probability interface retains conditional next-site probability: Assign a conditional score to the next observed site under an anchor hypothesis.
The product sequence likelihood interface retains sequence likelihood: Combine sequential event scores for a candidate anchor.
The Bayesian anchor ranking interface retains anchor posterior: Rank candidate home cells under a uniform prior.
The history-weighted next-site mixture interface retains next-site score: Form a relative next-location surface by mixing anchors and historical prefixes.
The L1 coordinate error interface retains Manhattan error distance: Measure displacement between predicted center and the actual next event.
Process events chronologically, update the centroid and velocity recurrence, and retain the state available before each holdout.
Fit longitude and latitude velocity trends separately and use their slopes as acceleration components.
Forecast a center at the next-event time and place axis-aligned mean-error bounds around it.
Collect dated crime addresses, convert them to latitude-longitude pairs, preserve order, and record case provenance.
Discretize the hunting area, encode previously used cells, evaluate the distance-buffer kernel, and normalize for ranking.
Evaluate the full observed sequence under every possible anchor cell and rank the resulting likelihoods.
Mix candidate anchors and historical prefix states to score every possible next site.
Sort cells from highest to lowest jeopardy, stop when the known home is reached, and convert the searched fraction into area.
Place centrographic and RSC outputs on the same historical prefix, compare with the actual next event, and retain assumption failures.

dependency_graph.handoff: The previous centroid anchors the new event displacement.
The event velocity updates the centroid-motion state.
The velocity history supplies regression inputs for acceleration.
The fitted acceleration and current velocity enter the damped center forecast.
The forecast center is expanded into an operational next-site region.
Prior site use and anchor distance determine the local choice score.
Sequential kernel scores are multiplied under each anchor hypothesis.
The sequence likelihood ranks candidate homes under the stated prior.
The posterior interface is evaluated across the finite search grid.
The mixture score is computed for every candidate future cell.
Held-out centrographic centers are evaluated against the actual next event.
The ranked surface is converted into searched fraction and physical area.
The centrographic region is compared beside the RSC surface on a shared case prefix.

verification.summary: For Hillside Strangler data, kill j is withheld and predicted using only kills 1 through j-1, beginning with j=4.
verification.limitation: The actual next-event time is still used and only one series is tested.

verification.summary: Table 2 reports five exact Manhattan errors for successive held-out events.
verification.strength: Prevents the mean from hiding every individual holdout.
verification.limitation: No baseline, uncertainty interval, or alternate distance metric is supplied.

verification.summary: Tables 3 and 4 expose separate longitude and latitude regression data.
verification.strength: Makes the acceleration fitting inputs visible.
verification.limitation: Sample sizes are tiny and diagnostics are incomplete.

verification.summary: Figure 1 overlays predicted centers, actual events, and diamond regions across the Hillside sequence.
verification.strength: Connects numeric errors to spatial direction and coverage.
verification.limitation: The diamond is not probability calibrated.

verification.summary: The Berkowitz jeopardy surface is checked against both Bronx and Yonkers residences.
verification.strength: Reveals sensitivity to a changed residence within one offender history.
verification.limitation: The Yonkers domain is enlarged after the fact.

verification.summary: Tables 5 and 6 translate ranked cells into Hit Score and Search Area for three home targets.
verification.strength: Connects ranking to searched land area.
verification.limitation: Boundary and resolution sensitivity are not tested.

verification.summary: Figure 4 compares an RSC seventh-event surface with the actual Berkowitz event.
verification.strength: Provides a qualitative held-out next-site test.
verification.limitation: It is a single example without a numeric next-site score.

verification.summary: Figures 5 and 6 place both models on the DC Sniper sequence.
verification.strength: Exposes repeated-location and same-day-event violations rather than reporting only successes.
verification.limitation: No repaired variants are rerun on the same case.

verification.summary: The Discussion compares the claimed decreasing-error pattern against event-level values.
verification.strength: Allows narrative claims to be checked against the table.
verification.limitation: The paper itself misses the increase at kill 6 and the mean discrepancy.

verification.summary: RSC performance is compared with random search through a chi-square claim.
verification.strength: Attempts to supply an external baseline.
verification.limitation: The statistical construction and dependence assumptions are undocumented.

verification.summary: The two models' distinct outputs are discussed as complementary police information.
verification.strength: Preserves separate home and next-event decision roles.
verification.limitation: No fused rule or joint validation is estimated.

results_trace.summary: Berkowitz Bronx uses 1414 square kilometers, 18.1 percent Hit Score, and 255 square kilometers Search Area.
Berkowitz Yonkers uses 2514 square kilometers, 63.2 percent Hit Score, and 1588 square kilometers Search Area.
Buono-Bianchi uses 2721 square kilometers, 13.9 percent Hit Score, and 379 square kilometers Search Area.
Neither model predicts the actual final DC Sniper event; repeated locations break the RSC rule and same-day events break the centrographic velocity.
The five reported Hillside errors average about 15.15 km and do not decrease monotonically.

contributions.summary: Turns a time-ordered crime centroid into a recursive motion state.
Adds damped velocity and acceleration so the forecast stops at long horizons.
Frames geographic profiling as a rational location-choice problem.
Builds a home jeopardy surface from sequential distance-buffer likelihoods.
Extends the anchor mixture to a relative next-site surface.
Uses both point error and searched-area metrics for operational interpretation.

writing_logic.summary: Summary chain: police task -> sparse data -> familiar-area assumptions -> centrographic forecast -> rational-choice surface -> historical tests -> limitations -> starting-point use.
Introduction chain: scarce serial-killer data -> two targets -> complementary models -> partial-series simulation -> section roadmap.
Background chain: operational definition -> home proximity evidence -> clustering -> anchor premise -> existing geographic profiling.
Literature chain: distance decay and buffers -> centroid precedents -> crime-pattern and rational-choice theory -> two model adaptations.
Centrographic chain: assumptions -> centroid -> event velocity -> momentum recurrence -> acceleration -> damped forecast -> prediction diamond.
RSC chain: utility and simplex -> implicit choice -> binary risk -> inverse-distance kernel -> sequence likelihood -> anchor posterior -> next-site mixture.
Evaluation chain: source and geocode data -> chronological holdouts -> error table and figure -> jeopardy surfaces -> Hit Score and Search Area -> DC Sniper countercase.
Discussion chain: interpret case results -> identify parameter and assumption failures -> qualify claims -> propose repairs -> joint-use boundary.
Executive chain: police inputs -> two outputs -> strengths and weaknesses -> map interpretation -> combined operational use.

language_observations.summary: The opening uses a vivid police scenario, then immediately replaces drama with a precise input-output contract.
Each model receives one parallel paragraph with motivation, mechanism, and target.
The Introduction closes every promise with a forward section reference, making the roadmap auditable.
Definitions, empirical percentages, and modeling consequences are placed in the same paragraph chain.
Kinematics is introduced through quoted vocabulary and then translated into explicit recurrences.
The phrase rational serial criminal is bounded so rationality means goal-directed choice rather than moral approval or perfect information.
To summarize marks the point where behavioral prose becomes a formal choice interface.
The Results section states forecast origin and metric before interpreting performance.
The Discussion alternates a positive result with its sensitivity or assumption failure.
The Executive Summary translates surfaces and diamonds into where-to-search language while retaining model-specific caveats.

visualization_observations.summary: Shows the complete task-assumption-two-model-test-boundary chain before the full paper.
Confirms title, team number, date, internal pagination, and the compact dual-model contract.
Preserves ordered dates, addresses, and latitude-longitude coordinates used by the simulations.
Reports the five Hillside Strangler next-event Manhattan errors used in the discussion.
Displays the x-direction velocity regression inputs and fit summary.
Displays the y-direction velocity regression inputs and fit summary.
Overlays observed sites, predicted centers, actual next events, and diamond regions across holdouts.
Shows shooting sites, candidate-home ranking, and both Bronx and Yonkers residences.
Converts two possible residences into hunting area, Hit Score, and Search Area values.
Reports the corresponding hunting area and search burden for one offender home.
Shows attack sites, the categorical home-likelihood field, and the known residence.
Displays the RSC next-site surface and actual held-out event for a qualitative check.
Shows that the predicted region does not contain the actual later event.
Shows the failed RSC next-site prediction under repeated-location data.
Translates model inputs, interpretations, strengths, and limitations for police readers.
Connects diamonds and contour plots to joint search-area narrowing and operational caution.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A complete dual-model summary plausibly improves traceability without establishing validity.
Sequential holdout maps plausibly help judges connect equations to spatial consequences.
Search Area plausibly improves operational relevance, while domain sensitivity limits credibility.

weaknesses.summary: The analysis assumes that all events in a supplied series belong to one offender, but linkage uncertainty is not modeled.
A single stationary home base is assumed; the Berkowitz residence change directly demonstrates the resulting failure mode.
A uniform prior over candidate homes assigns positive mass to water and other uninhabitable cells unless an external mask is added.
The address-to-coordinate and coordinate-to-kilometer workflow does not document projection, geocoder version, or positional error.
A discrete running centroid is differentiated as a continuous curve without defining an interpolation between event times.
Same-day events create a zero time denominator and infinite event velocity; the issue is acknowledged only after the DC Sniper failure.
Momentum conservation and perfectly inelastic collision are analogies for a mean recurrence, not established laws of offender behavior.
The acceleration regressions use very few points, so slope estimates and extrapolations are unstable.
The discussion describes an R-squared value as about 90 percent correlation, conflating coefficient of determination and correlation.
The choice beta=ln(15)/mean interval has no behavioral derivation, fitted loss, external calibration, or sensitivity analysis.
Holdout prediction evaluates the center at the actual next-event time, information that would not be known at deployment.
The axis-wise mean-error diamond is not calibrated as a coverage region and has no stated probability interpretation.
The constrained utility optimization omits a Lagrange multiplier and incorrectly states partial U over partial p_i equals zero as the full first-order condition.
The implicit-function argument lacks the required non-singular Jacobian and explicit treatment of the simplex constraint.
Leaving utility and the choice functions arbitrary makes the general model weakly identified before the paper selects a kernel.
Binary prior-use risk forces an already used location to zero probability, an assumption violated by the DC Sniper sequence.
The kernel sets the exact anchor cell to zero and combines buffer and normalization terms without fully documenting their construction.
The product likelihood assumes a conditional generation structure that is neither estimated nor empirically checked.
The next-site double sum mixes multiple prefix states and anchor hypotheses without a clear normalization or forecast-time interpretation.
Several outputs are called probabilities although the implementation and evaluation mainly establish relative rankings.
Wikipedia, newspaper, and web addresses are used without a reproducible snapshot, geocoding log, or source-error assessment.
Berkowitz shooting sites and Hillside Strangler body-disposal sites represent different behavioral targets but are treated under one interface.
Physical page 11 contains consecutive headings '4 Data' and '5 Data', exposing an unresolved structural editing error.
Hit Score changes with hunting-area boundary and grid resolution, neither of which receives a sensitivity study.
The Yonkers hunting area is explicitly enlarged to include the known home, making that reported evaluation partly outcome-informed.
The chi-square goodness-of-fit comparison does not state samples, bins, degrees of freedom, dependence treatment, or implementation.
Three dependent case scores do not support the broad claim that the model is statistically superior to random search.
Next-event validation is dominated by qualitative single-holdout maps rather than repeated rolling-origin tests.
Jeopardy maps use blue, red, green, and purple categories without a continuous color bar or numeric probability scale.
The claim that error decreases after every added crime conflicts with Table 2, where the sixth-event error rises sharply.
The five Table 2 errors average about 15.15 km, not the 15.12 km stated in the discussion.
The Python simulation code and Excel macros are not supplied, preventing exact reproduction.
The Combined Models section displays outputs side by side but does not estimate or validate a fused decision rule.
The recommendation that police can fill population and geography gaps provides no formal adjustment protocol, calibration check, or safety rule.

independent_extensions.summary: Model linkage and moving-anchor uncertainty instead of assuming one stationary offender home.
Use projected coordinates, explicit interpolation, nonzero-time handling, and nested calibration for beta and acceleration.
Replace the zero-repeat binary kernel with a fitted soft-risk model and a geographic feasibility mask.
Version case sources, geocoding, projections, and forecast-origin timestamps so every simulation is reproducible.
Use rolling origins, simple baselines, uncertainty, calibration, grid sensitivity, and predeclared domains for both targets.
Estimate and validate a fused decision rule with abstention when repeated sites, same-day events, or moved anchors are detected.

candidate_rule_impacts.action: retain the task-contract, assumption-motivation, parallel dual-model preview, analogy-to-formalism, and result-countercase language mechanisms
retain ordered event coordinates and dates only with linkage, provenance, geocoding, projection, and forecast-availability metadata
retain complete centroid-state and choice-likelihood interfaces with units, chronology, domain, and target explicit
distinguish physical analogies and normalized rankings from calibrated behavioral probabilities
retain modular damping and kernel choices only with estimation, sensitivity, feasibility masks, and assumption diagnostics
retain chronological holdouts and resource metrics while requiring deployment-available time, baselines, rolling origins, uncertainty, and fixed domains
use moved-anchor, repeated-location, same-day-event, and domain-sensitivity cases as mandatory reliability diagnostics
retain event overlays and paired case maps while requiring quantitative color bars, truth markers, common scales, and caption-data checks
translate center error and ranked surfaces into bounded search actions only after units, area, capacity, and abstention rules are explicit
compare or combine model families only on the same event prefix, forecast time, domain, target, metric, and uncertainty protocol
